title: WeatherNext 3: Raw-Observation AI Global Weather Model Reaches Hourly 0.1° Resolution
whyItMatters: WeatherNext 3 breaks AI weather models’ reliance on 6-hourly physics analysis grids—ingesting live geostationary satellite mosaics to issue hourly 0.1° global forecasts and direct unseen-station predictions.
summary: Posted on September 3, 2026 (arXiv:2609.03582) and followed on November 13, 2026 by the open release of its foundational Earth-science training datasets (SatWeave and PARDIG), Google DeepMind’s WeatherNext 3 overcomes the two core bottlenecks of prior AI weather models: coarse spatial/temporal grids and exclusive dependence on physics-based reanalysis initialization. By directly ingesting low-latency global geostationary satellite mosaics (SatWeave) alongside AI-derived global precipitation estimates (PARDIG, which improves hourly light-to-moderate precipitation detection >30% over NASA IMERG-Final), WeatherNext 3 generates new global probabilistic forecasts every hour—rather than every 6 hours—at 0.1° spatial resolution and hourly time steps matching top physics-based global models. Moving beyond gridded analysis variables, it directly predicts satellite precipitation, tropical cyclones, and sparse weather-station 2m temperature and dewpoint at arbitrary unseen locations conditioned on local geography.
technicalHighlights: Breaks AI weather forecasting’s analysis-only barrier by ingesting live geostationary satellite observations (SatWeave) to issue new global forecasts every hour instead of every 6 hours.
Matches physics-based global models at 0.1° spatial resolution and hourly time steps for single-level fields including solar radiation and cloud cover.
Directly models satellite precipitation (via PARDIG, >30% CSI gain over IMERG-Final), tropical cyclones, and sparse ground stations—cutting 2m temperature/dewpoint error at unseen stations.
caveats: Preprint posted September 2026 under active community review; operational meteorological agencies continue to evaluate extreme-event calibration alongside numerical assimilation pipelines.

scoreRationale.foundational: Unifies data assimilation, medium-range forecasting, and local station post-processing into a single end-to-end observation-driven global weather model.
scoreRationale.ripple: Open release of SatWeave and PARDIG (1999–2026 archive + live feeds) catalyzes hydrology, flood, solar-energy, and localized climate forecasting worldwide.
scoreRationale.verification: Comprehensive quantitative verification across global benchmarks, unseen weather stations, and US/Europe/Japan ground radar networks; journal peer review is pending.
scoreRationale.velocity: Updates global 0.1° probabilistic forecasts hourly from live satellite data at a tiny fraction of numerical assimilation compute.
